reason_for_new_version: Step 75's windowed-mean gates were leak-free but could not distinguish a duty-cycled attack from an occasional benign burst of similar peak magnitude. v5.0 uses a rate-of-exceedance mechanism instead, which measures how often a metric is elevated rather than its smoothed average.
score_model: unchanged from Step 54 (v3 directional one-sided MEWMA/T2 pressure score)
confirmation_rule: unchanged from Step 55 (6-of-8 confirmed upper-control states)

cpu.derivation: sample max of pooled N1+N2+N3 per-second raw values; nonparametric one-sided tolerance bound, 95% confidence that >= 99.9% of future clean per-second samples fall within bound (Wilks 1941), n=5400 >= 2995

m4.derivation: sample max of pooled N1+N2+N3 per-second raw values; nonparametric one-sided tolerance bound, 95% confidence that >= 99.9% of future clean per-second samples fall within bound (Wilks 1941), n=5316 >= 2995

tx.derivation: sample min of pooled N1+N2+N3 per-second raw values; nonparametric one-sided tolerance bound, 95% confidence that >= 99.9% of future clean per-second samples fall within bound (Wilks 1941), n=5400 >= 2995

m4_gate_excluded_reason: m4_memory_growth_bytes_per_s spikes to values physically inconsistent with the concurrent m3_memory_working_set_bytes trajectory on BOTH benign (A5, 521167 bytes/s peak vs ~250KB/10s actual M3 change) and attack (R6, >1000000 bytes/s peak vs a few hundred KB/10s actual M3 change) data, with no quality/reset flag raised. Treated as an unreliable feature, not tuned around.
tx_gate_excluded_reason: Contributes zero incremental TPR or latency on R1/R6 once the CPU gate is present, while adding ~2.8pp FPR on A5 (development). Retained in the manifest as a computed diagnostic column only.
compromise_policy: COMPROMISED requires corroborating evidence outside this resource score.
